--- title: "Rapid automatized naming: repeated long objects" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · RAN_OBJETOS_REPETIDOS_LARGOS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (B · Rapid naming; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea RAN_OBJETOS_REPETIDOS_LARGOS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Denominación rápida de objetos repetidos (largos)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/RAN_OBJETOS_REPETIDOS_LARGOS.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Rapid automatized naming: repeated long objects, from age 7 to 8 (1,756 administrations in 3 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .45. AUC .64–.74 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1945 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | — | | Task family | B · Rapid naming | | Score | Time (s; lower is better) | | Instructions (platform) | La tarea consiste en nombrar los objetos que aparecen en la pantalla lo más rápido que se pueda, tratando de no equivocarse. Se presenta una plantilla con 3 filas de 6 imágenes. *(Spanish)* | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_ran.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework Rapid naming of pictures measures how quickly the child retrieves and says, in series, very familiar names; it is one of the best predictors of reading fluency. The variants change: - the **phonological similarity** of the names: same initial syllable, same initial phoneme, or unrelated names (control); - the **length** of the names: short or long; - **repetition**: five repeated pictures or varied pictures, on a card or one at a time. **What the evidence says:** - **RAN predicts reading, also with pictures and before reading.** A meta-analysis of 137 studies (28,826 participants) finds a moderate to strong relation (r = .43). Stimulus type is one of the most influential moderators [@araujo2014ran]. In a three-year longitudinal study, non-alphanumeric RAN measured before reading instruction predicted fluency growth, with no reverse effect of reading on RAN [@lervag2009ran]. - **In Spanish, pictures and alphanumeric stimuli form distinct factors.** In 874 Spanish children from Grade 2 to Grade 6, RAN tasks group into an alphanumeric and a non-alphanumeric factor, stable across grades [@rodriguez2015ran]. - **Phonological similarity adds a load that affects dyslexia more, but with letters.** Readers with dyslexia are more impaired than others when adjacent letters sound similar [@jones2013ran]. We have not found studies that manipulate picture names in this way: this variant is specific to the platform and its interpretation is, for now, a hypothesis. - **Format matters.** In Grade 1, serial RAN is more strongly related to reading than discrete RAN (one stimulus at a time) [@dejong2011discrete]. **What our data show.** These are class B and C tasks, with few sessions per variant: - **Stability.** ρ = .33 (control), .42 (same syllable) and .41 (same phoneme) across terms from age 4 to 6; .45 for the long versions at ages 7 to 8. - **Validity.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC from .55 to .72 at ages 4 to 6 and from .57 to .74 at ages 7–8. Against later low comprehension, only .52 to .63. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, maximum AUC of .70. - **Phonological similarity.** The same-phoneme version reaches .72 at age 6, compared with .65–.67 for the control, but the intervals overlap: there is no clear advantage in manipulating phonology. - **Caution.** Mean times change a lot between sessions of the same school year (in the control version, 25.5 s at 4.1 and 44.5 s at 4.2). Norms must be computed by session and the administered version reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 7.1| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 730| 223| 506| 31| | 7.2| 2012| 904|2019/20 | 191| 187| 0| 11| | 8.1| 2011| 900|2019/20 | 369| 0| 369| 25| | 8.3| 2010| 640|2018/19 | 466| 103| 362| 24| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 7.1| 223| 2010| 20.28| 4.98| 19.52| 1.24|NA |NA | | 7.2| 187| 2012| 19.09| 4.10| 18.41| 0.78|NA |NA | | 8.3| 103| 2010| 17.02| 4.24| 16.38| 1.71|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in seconds). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 7.1| 223|12.6–37.5 |12.3–38.5 | | | 7.2| 187|12.3–30.7 |12.3–33.3 | | | 8.3| 103|11.6–32.3 |11.5–35.1 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .45 (median .45, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency from item-level responses is missing. As a timed task, stability is the preferred reliability estimate. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 7.1| 8.3| 375| 0.43| 0.45| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Rapid naming (RAN)), r = .38–.59. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (7.1, r = .39); Word and text reading (7.2, r = .37); Word and text reading (8.1, r = .33); Word and text reading (8.3, r = .43). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .64–.74. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .56–.58. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_RAN_OBJETOS_REPETIDOS_LARGOS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .54–.70 (3 time points; 223–254 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:| | 7.1| 223| 2010| 29.8| 27.0| 24.6| 22.5| 19.5| 16.7| 14.9| | 7.2| 187| 2012| 26.9| 24.6| 23.3| 21.3| 18.4| 16.0| 14.5| | 8.1| 369| 2011| 24.5| 22.1| 20.7| 19.5| 17.2| 15.4| 13.8| | 8.3| 103| 2010| 23.6| 21.7| 20.7| 19.1| 16.4| 14.1| 12.8| In rapid naming, less time is better: P10 is the time of the slowest 10%. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_RAN_OBJETOS_REPETIDOS_LARGOS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 690| 0.191| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 730| 0.083| 0.261| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 729| 0.010| 0.778| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 730| 0.076| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.2| 189| 0.069| 0.345| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.2| 191| 0.024| 0.871| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.2| 191| 0.164| 0.024| |School (ICC) | 7.2| 191| 0.058| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.1| 368| 0.029| 0.586| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.1| 369| -0.020| 0.845| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.1| 368| -0.016| 0.760| |School (ICC) | 8.1| 369| 0.000| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.3| 466| 0.168| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.3| 459| 0.028| 0.770| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.3| 458| 0.022| 0.639| |School (ICC) | 8.3| 466| 0.091| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Rapid automatized naming: repeated long objects” (code 1945; DIS-ESP battery) assesses rapid automatized naming (lexical access). The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 4 sessions, from 7 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the completion time (seconds). Stability across time points was ρ = .45. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .56–.58. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
